text:
jessica (support): pinging the group — customer reported sustained 429s on their Dedicated pool starting ~08:30 UTC after we ran the billing plan migration. They have reserved capacity and were previously fine.
harper (sre): thanks — do we have request IDs or sample logs?
jessica (support): pasted a snippet from their token-level logs: `rate_key=acct_12345; plan=enterprise-pro; denom_minutes=60; allowed_units=1200` but the pool was enforcing `denom=3600` (per-hour) which effectively dropped their throughput.
sanjay (eng-infra): that sounds like a denom translation mismatch from the legacy plan importer. I can grep the migration job logs.
ops-bot: migration-job-457 completed 2026-03-10T02:12:03Z, status=SUCCESS, steps=5
maya (product): was there a recent change to smoothing/autoscale thresholds? Customer thinks autoscale didn't kick.
harper (sre): autoscale looks fine — nodes were healthy and not saturated. The signal shows many requests being rejected by the per-tenant rate limiter before the pool-level queue.
sanjay (eng-infra): found the mapping: migration script accidentally preserved `unit=minutes` as `denom_seconds=minutes` instead of converting to seconds. In config it became `denom=60` instead of `denom=3600` for the plan tag, which then triggered a fallback and applied the conservative per-hour enforcement in the dedicated rate adapter. Patch incoming.
jessica (support): repro steps for internal devs: 1) import legacy plan JSON with `rate_unit: minutes` 2) run `bin/migrate-plans --dry-run` 3) observe translation to `denom=60` in DB 4) send request flood with API key -> 429s. Example curl for flooding test:
```bash
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer acct_12345_key" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null & done
```
harper (sre): logs around reject show: `limiter=per_tenant v=1 reject=true key=acct_12345 denom=60 units=1200 window_start=...` then the pool adapter shows `compatible_variant=fallback-low-qps`.
maya (product): recommend short-term: bump customer's per-tenant limit to match expected throughput and roll a hotfix to migration. Long-term: add unit sanity checks and end-to-end migration test.
sanjay (eng-infra): I'm pushing a hotfix to treat legacy `minutes` -> denom_seconds=3600 when plan level tag = "hourly-legacy". Also adding a migration validation hook. Rolling to staging now.
ops-bot: deploy-job-901 started by sanjay, status=IN_PROGRESS
jessica (support): told customer we've isolated a translation bug and ETA for mitigation ~30-45m. They patched their app to throttle but want the backend fixed.
harper (sre): once hotfix is live we'll run a focused replay against their API key and confirm 429s stop without adding pool capacity. I can coordinate timing with oncall.
sanjay (eng-infra): hotfix deployed to staging, passing smoke. Scheduling prod deploy in 10m (quiet window).
ops-bot: deploy-job-901 status=SUCCESS job_url=https://ci.redwood.dev/901
maya (product): thanks team. Action items: sanjay -> prod hotfix + migration validation (PR#4022), harper -> post-deploy replay + telemetry check, jessica -> confirm with customer and keep them in loop.
jessica (support): customer confirmed improvement after our interim per-tenant bump; will watch for recurrence. Closing the loop once post-deploy checks are green. :thumbsup:
